Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill for a shoulder, sausages and sides for about twelve
Resource limits: one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner, one cooler for holding, two cooks.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill

Two cooks, one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner and a cooler for holding. The pork owns the smoker all day; everything else happens in the last two hours.

Pork shoulder
Light the smoker and bring it to 250°F; 45 minutes. While it comes up, trim the shoulder and rub it heavily with salt, pepper and paprika; 25 minutes. Put the shoulder on once the smoker holds temperature and smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, until the bark is dark and set. Wrap it tightly in butcher paper; 10 minutes. Back on the smoker, wrapped, until the thickest part probes soft — usually another 3 hours, sometimes four. Hold it wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours; it will not get cold and it only gets better. Pull the meat by hand; 30 minutes.

Beans
When the pork goes into the cooler, fry the bacon and onion in the pot on the side burner for 12 minutes, then add the beans, molasses and a ladle of drippings and let them tick over on the lowest flame until you serve.

Slaw
Start the slaw at the same time. Shred the cabbage and carrot; 20 minutes. Whisk the buttermilk dressing; 8 minutes. Dress the slaw and put it in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes so the cabbage softens.

Grill
Light the kettle an hour before you eat; 25 minutes to a clean bed of coals. Grill the sausages for 14 minutes. Grill the corn for 10 minutes. Toast the buns for 3 minutes, last, so they stay warm.

Table
Set out plates, pickles and sauce once the buns are off; 10 minutes. Call everyone over when both cooks say it is ready; 5 minutes to lay it all out.
>>>

This makes a backyard barbecue for about twelve people: a pork shoulder smoked unwrapped for six hours, wrapped and smoked another three to four hours, then held wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours before pulling; beans are cooked on the side burner and held at a low simmer, slaw is chilled for at least 45 minutes, and sausages, corn, and buns are cooked on the kettle grill near serving time, with the buns toasted last. No finishing time was given, so the work should finish as early as the required cooking and holding periods allow. The setup has one offset smoker dedicated to the pork, one kettle grill, one side burner, one cooler for holding, and two cooks; the smoker must reach 250°F before the shoulder goes on, the grill should be lit about an hour before eating, and the table is set after the buns are done and the food is ready.

A track is one sequential line of work, so steps on the same track cannot overlap; simultaneous work belongs on separate tracks. Each step has exactly one duration kind: fixed with seconds, variable with minimum, maximum, and default seconds, or indefinite until the user ends it. A start trigger connects a step to the program clock, another step, a manual action, an abort, or a compound condition. Step IDs must be unique across the entire program, and every task used by a step must have a matching resource constraint whose `maxConcurrent` limits simultaneous use. Repeated work is represented once with `replicates`, using serial, parallel, or stagger mode rather than copied steps, with `each` for per-instance follow-up, `all` for a barrier, and `maxInFlight` when a holding area has limited capacity. This barbecue needs one smoker, one grill, one side burner, one cooler, two cooks, and shared preparation and serving capacity for the parallel work.

- `prep`: maxConcurrent 2

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or cook_recipe), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
